routes.how: He trips through a hole in the party floor and falls into pure blackness, where Flashing Lights finds him falling or floating.
The tambourine he throws leaves through the shattered window and tumbles through black space toward the chapel; the POET himself does not travel (he is absent from the next poem).
Cut to the POET standing on the same shore at night among the washed-up broken pieces (Nevermore).
'Now go.' - still night, he walks on through the field into the welcoming parade of afro-futuristic ancestors (Bloodlines).
Still night, he sees the entrance to Atlantis and goes in; the stretch from parade to gate is not written (inferred: he walks down the path, possibly escorted).
After the voiceover he wanders the city and finally arrives at a house people are entering; he enters (the DJ Turn Me Up house party).
He leaves the house party / poetry reading for an open-air rooftop club; the treatment does not say how he gets there (inferred: up the stairs to a nearby or same-building roof).
With no voice-over he leaves the club and walks down the street below, crowds on the sidewalk fawning over him — the street where Yet, Heard begins.
He does not travel: the EX turns to haze on the sidewalk, and the POET is left alone on the same sidewalk beside a parked motorcycle where Magic Ride opens.
He rides back to the shore at the decaying chapel, where he begins to build a new, clean white temple (New Day / 'Temple').
Ellipsis 'Decades later': the same temple fills with friends and events (the treatment's 'Temple (Cont.)' runs straight into Reunion).
Daytime/sunlight: the POET wanders out of the new temple and around the harbor to a cafe.
Haze gathers on the water and grows; Atlantis, the new temple and the harbor dissolve into haze, which envelops the POET from the ground up while he resists.
Door closes. The film ends inside the vintage party where the fall began — a loop, not a return home.
